title: ToeFX Light Therapy for Chronic Venous Leg Ulcers
official: Adjunctive ToeFX Photodynamic Therapy for Chronic Venous Leg Ulcers: A Single-Arm, Open-Label Pilot Feasibility Study
summary:
Chronic venous leg ulcers can be painful and prone to infection. They can significantly limit a patient's function, mobility and quality of life.

A major contributor to delayed ulcer healing is persistent bacteria. Treatments that can penetrate the bacteria's protective outer shield to kill and clear the bacteria are important for helping ulcers heal more quickly.

The purpose of this pilot study is to test a topical study treatment (called ClearToe Serum®) plus two types of light (red and blue-purple light) in the treatment of chronic venous ulcers.

This is an open-label single-arm pilot study. All participants will receive the test treatment as well as standard or care treatment for their chronic venous ulcer. Participants will receive study treatments one per week for up to 12 weeks, or until their ulcer is healed.

The main objectives are to assess adherence to the one-per-week study treatments, and to note any study device-related, study treatment-related, or serious adverse events, or adverse events that lead to stopping study treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Able to attend weekly visits for up to 12 weeks
* Chronic venous leg ulcer (CEAP C6) of the lower extremity
* Ulcer duration of 4 weeks or more
* Ulcer size between 1 cm² and 20 cm² at baseline
* Receiving standard-of-care compression therapy, or eligible to initiate it
* Able to provide informed consent and comply with study procedures

Exclusion Criteria:

* Wound location or anatomy not compatible with the ToeFX photodynamic therapy device
* Systemic infection (e.g., fever, sepsis, spreading cellulitis) or wound requiring systemic antibiotics
* Necrotic tissue over 25% of the wound bed, exposed bone or tendon, deep abscess, osteomyelitis or gangrene
* Severe ischemia (ABI below 0.5) or poorly controlled diabetes (HbA1c above 10%)
* Heavy exudate requiring negative-pressure wound therapy
* Known photosensitivity or allergy to methylene blue or light-based therapies
* Immunosuppressive therapy, radiation or chemotherapy within the past 3 months, or active malignancy
* Pregnancy or lactation
* Known Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency
* Participation in another interventional study within 30 days of screening
